title: The first khatm
hookLine: the last page, a finger under the line, a family pretending not to listen

cards: A child sits cross-legged with a big book on a little wooden stand, a finger moving under the lines, voice careful. The teacher leans in. The family is in the doorway, pretending not to listen.
It's the last page. A few short surahs left, then the final line of al-Nas, and it's done: the whole Qur'an, read through, out loud.
In some homes and mosques, that moment gets a party: new clothes, sweets, guests, the child reading the closing surahs in front of everyone.

teach.b: Khatm means a completion: a full reading of the Qur'an, from the opening to the end. Adults do it too, alone or together, sometimes over a single month.
But a child's first khatm can take years of small daily lessons to reach. Why celebrate it? A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase: the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.
The child has learned, and someone, a parent, a teacher, an imam, has taught. A khatm party honors both halves of that sentence at once. Second, the struggle counts.

teach.h: THE HALTING READER: A DOUBLE REWARD.
teach.b: In Bukhari and Muslim, in paraphrase: the one who is skilled at reciting the Qur'an is with the noble, righteous scribes, and the one who recites it haltingly, finding it hard, has a double reward.
Hear that from the child's side. Every stumble over a long word wasn't wasted; in this hadith, the struggling reader is the one promised two rewards. Third, the book says it can be carried.

In surah al-Qamar, in Pickthall's translation: "And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember." A child at a little stand, closing the last page, is that verse in a living room. Fourth, it doesn't really end.
Some families mark the khatm by having the child turn straight back to the beginning and read al-Fatiha again, right there.
Finish, and start again. The celebration isn't for being done. It's for being on the way.

how: In some Muslim communities, a child who finishes reading the whole Qur'an for the first time is honored with a gathering, where the child recites the closing surahs and the family thanks the teacher; the customs and names vary by culture.

games.q: you're the teacher. on the very last page, in front of the whole family, the child stumbles on a long word. what do you do?
o: take over and read it yourself.
let them work through it; the struggle counts.
games.why: in the hadith, the one who recites haltingly, finding it hard, has a double reward. the stumble is part of the gift.

practice: Bring to mind a child who has finished something lately, a book, a school year, the alphabet, or remember your own first finish and who was there for it.
Think of words that honor the work, not just the result: I saw how hard you worked. If you pray, thank Allah for their learning in your own words; if not, just let yourself be glad for them.

wordCard.voice: The first khatm. A child's first complete reading of the Qur'an, and the celebration some families give it. Today's word.
